study.title: Deep learning-based classification of DSA image sequences of patients with acute ischemic stroke
study.venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery

imaging.modality_detail: 2D cerebral DSA sequences acquired simultaneously in posterior-anterior (PA) and lateral (LAT) views during thrombectomy; 1024 x 1024 pixels
imaging.territory_detail: Cerebrovasculature, perfusion territory of the internal carotid artery (acute ischemic stroke, thrombectomy); vertebral and external carotid-only sequences excluded

data_released.detail: Due to data protection reasons, the DSA data set cannot be published.

annotation.annotator_expertise: experienced neuroradiologists; discordant sequences re-annotated jointly
annotation.inter_rater_value: Interobserver variability of thrombus position annotation 23 +/- 28 image pixels (2% +/- 3% of image width)

task.task_description: Binary classification of DSA sequences (and PA+LAT sequence pairs) into thrombus-free vs non-thrombus-free (thrombus-yes-no-classification) using CNN feature extractors combined with bidirectional GRU/LSTM networks.
task.clinical_application: Intraprocedural alerting during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke to reduce the risk of overlooking new thrombi/emboli

architecture_names: Ensemble of four network variants (two per view)

temporal_evidence.quote: The extracted features served as input to the LSTM or GRU network, which outputted the classification result

method.pretraining: ImageNet (Torchvision) or ImageNet-21k (timm, EfficientNetV2) pretrained CNN backbones, fine-tuned end-to-end
method.class_imbalance_handling: Matthews correlation coefficient used as model selection criterion due to unbalanced classes (72% positives)

model_weights_available.detail: Trained network models published on the Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/n8k4r/)

G1.quote: To improve the classification performance and the generalizability, a substantially larger amount of multi-center training data would be required.

G2.quote: As our retrospective study was based on single-center DSA imaging data, the trained neural networks could be less generalizable with respect to DSA data of other stroke units.

G3.quote: we addressed the challenge of automatically identifying spatio-temporal perfusion abnormalities caused by thrombi in DSA image sequences of variable sequence length

G5.quote: this is related to the high interobserver variability of the thrombus position annotation

G6.quote: only a prospective study can analyze how the trained neural networks will perform in clinical practice

G9.quote: the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) [5] does not tend to overestimate the classification performance especially for an unbalanced binary class distribution

G10.quote: Due to data protection reasons, the DSA data set cannot be published.

other_limitations: Small, inconspicuous distal perfusion abnormalities with uncertain annotation mostly misclassified as thrombus-free (false negatives)
future_work: Prospective study of performance in clinical practice
Automatic thrombus detection/localization in DSA images
Determine handling of annotation variability and suitable evaluation metrics for thrombus detection
